# Overview

I am a climate scientist and machine learning researcher bridging the gap between statistical data science and real-world climate challenges. 

Currently, I am a Research Fellow at Georgetown University’s **Earth Commons Institute**, where I develop open-source machine learning and Bayesian frameworks to improve long-term climate risk forecasts and hazard emergence detection. My work integrates global climate models, high-performance computing, and spatial statistics to quantify uncertainty across complex climate systems.

Previously, I completed my Ph.D. at the **IBS Center for Climate Physics**, analyzing ultra-high-resolution simulations on global supercomputers to track extreme weather events. Beyond core research, I build open-source tools for climate risk assessment and create high-impact climate data visualizations.

I enjoy collaborating across disciplines, advancing open climate data science, and communicating complex science clearly. Feel free to explore my research or reach out to connect!
